title: Compatible etale scheme charts for infinitesimal pushouts
statement: Work with algebraic spaces over a scheme $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A thickening is a representable closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism on underlying spaces; closed immersions are tested after base change to schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The topology of an algebraic space is the quotient topology from a representable surjective etale scheme atlas. An affine map is representable and its scheme base changes have affine inverse images of affine opens. Let $T\to T^+$ be a thickening of schemes and $T\to S$ an affine scheme morphism over $B$. Let $P=S\amalg_T T^+$, let $X/S$, $Y/T^+$ be algebraic spaces and fix $\phi:X\times_S T\simeq Y\times_{T^+}T$. Write $U=X\times_S T$ and $Z=X\amalg_U Y$ for the algebraic-space pushout [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout]. For any scheme $X_1$ and representable surjective etale map $X_1\to X$, there exist a scheme $Y_1$, a representable surjective etale map $Y_1\to Y$, and an isomorphism $$X_1\times_S T\simeq Y_1\times_{T^+}T$$ over $U$, compatible with $\phi$. For any such compatible pair of scheme covers, set $U_1=X_1\times_S T$ and form the scheme pushout $Z_1=X_1\amalg_{U_1}Y_1$. The induced map $Z_1\to Z$ is representable surjective etale, and the two squares with horizontal maps $X_1\to Z_1$, $X\to Z$ and $Y_1\to Z_1$, $Y\to Z$ and vertical cover maps are cartesian. No flatness or local finite presentation is assumed.

proof.text: The map $U\to Y$ is the base change of $T\hookrightarrow T^+$, hence a thickening. On every scheme base change to $X$, the map $U\to X$ is a scheme base change of the affine map $T\to S$, so the affine-morphism permanence lemma makes it affine. Thus $U_1=X_1\times_XU=X_1\times_ST$ is a scheme and $U_1\to U$ is representable surjective etale. Apply the equivalence on etale scheme objects across $U\hookrightarrow Y$ to obtain a scheme $Y_1$ etale over $Y$ and the specified isomorphism $Y_1\times_YU\cong U_1$. Its composite with $U\cong Y\times_{T^+}T$ gives the required compatibility with $\phi$. The map $U_1\hookrightarrow Y_1$ is a thickening. Both horizontal maps in its square over $U\hookrightarrow Y$ are homeomorphisms, and $U_1\to U$ is surjective, so $Y_1\to Y$ is surjective too. This proves existence of a compatible pair.

Now fix any compatible pair $(X_1,Y_1)$ of the statement. Applied to $U\hookrightarrow Y$ and the affine map $U\to X$, the geometric-pushout lemma says that $X\hookrightarrow Z$ is a thickening. Apply the etale scheme-object equivalence to this thickening and the given $X_1\to X$: obtain a scheme $E$ and a representable etale map $e:E\to Z$ with a fixed isomorphism $E\times_ZX\cong X_1$ over $X$. The projection $X_1\to E$ is a thickening by base change. The two horizontal maps $X_1\to E$ and $X\to Z$ are homeomorphisms and $X_1\to X$ is surjective, so $e$ is surjective.

Set $E_Y=E\times_ZY$. The geometric-pushout lemma identifies $Y$ with $Z\times_PT^+$, where $P$ is the scheme pushout $S\amalg_TT^+$ and $Z\to P$ is the induced map. Hence $E_Y\cong E\times_Z(Z\times_PT^+)\cong E\times_PT^+$ is a fibre product of schemes, so $E_Y$ is a scheme; and $E_Y\to Y$ is representable etale as a base change of the representable etale map $E\to Z$. (The scheme property does not follow from representability of $E\to Z$ alone, since $Y$ is only an algebraic space.) Over $U$ its restriction is canonically $E\times_ZU\cong(E\times_ZX)\times_XU\cong U_1$, by the universal properties of the fibre products. The given compatibility identifies $Y_1\times_YU$ with this same $U_1$. Full faithfulness of the etale scheme-object equivalence for $U\hookrightarrow Y$ therefore lifts this isomorphism uniquely to $E_Y\cong Y_1$: lift the map and its inverse, whose composites are identities because restriction is faithful. These identifications respect the maps from $U_1$ by their construction.

proof.text: Apply etale base change of a pushout to $Z=X\amalg_UY$ and $E\to Z$. Step 3 identifies its three restricted objects with $X_1,U_1,Y_1$, so $E$ is their pushout in algebraic spaces. The scheme pushout $Z_1=X_1\amalg_{U_1}Y_1$ exists and is also their algebraic-space pushout: the thickening $U_1\hookrightarrow Y_1$ and affine map $U_1\to X_1$ satisfy the geometric-pushout lemma. The universal properties give inverse maps $Z_1\rightleftarrows E$ fixing both pieces; each composite is the identity since it agrees with it on both pieces. The induced map $Z_1\to Z$ is therefore $e$ under this isomorphism, since both maps agree on $X_1,Y_1$. It is representable surjective etale. Finally $E\times_ZX=X_1$ by step 2 and $E\times_ZY\cong Y_1$ by step 3, proving precisely the two asserted cartesian squares for this arbitrary compatible pair.
